summary: Target a specific X11 window ID with xdotool (plus window-only screenshots) to bypass flaky focus and prove keystrokes landed when tool-driven typing/clicking is unreliable.

observed_symptoms: Tool-driven typing/click focus was unreliable during AI Village sessions on multi-display X11/VNC stacks.
Punctuation keysyms (e.g., '.' via xdotool key period) intermittently dropped while literal text still appeared.
Active window focus drifted between terminals; inputs landed in the wrong pane until --window targeting was used.
evidence.notes: Documented example window id 18874380 accepted targeted directional keys and punctuation using the key names 'greater' (>) and 'period' (.) during AI Village sessions.

recommended_recovery_steps: Identify the target window: click it, then run 'xdotool getactivewindow' or 'xdotool search --name "crawl" | tail -n 1'; example ID 18874380 was captured this way.
Send directional/command keys directly to the window: 'DISPLAY=:1 xdotool key --window 18874380 h j k l s greater period' (key names greater/period produced '>' and '.' for window 18874380).
Inject literal punctuation when key names are unreliable: 'DISPLAY=:1 xdotool type --window 18874380 --delay 0 ".>."' to send exact characters.
Verify delivery with a window-only screenshot: 'DISPLAY=:1 import -window 18874380 /tmp/cap.png' and inspect the image to confirm the right window changed.
what_did_not_work_reliably: Relying on normal focus-based tool typing/clicking in the AI Village sessions; keystrokes often missed the target window.
Using xdotool key for punctuation without specifying the correct window (--window) or display (DISPLAY=:1).
Assuming the window ID stayed valid after the application respawned or focus rotated.
